chunks: And it is narrated from ʿĪsā ibn Shaqafiyy, and he was a sorcerer to whom people used to come, and he used to take payment for that. He said:

So I performed hajj and met Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام at Minā. I said to him, “May I be your ransom, I am a man whose profession was sorcery, and I used to take payment for it. I have performed hajj, and Allah, Mighty and Exalted, has blessed me with meeting you, and I have repented to Allah. Is there for me any way out regarding any part of it?”
So he عليه السلام said, “Yes: undo, and do not tie.”

key_terms.السِّحْرَ: sorcery; the unlawful practice the man formerly worked in
key_terms.الْأَجْرَ: payment or wage taken in exchange for that practice
key_terms.تَعْقِدْ: tie; meaning not to perform or initiate binding spells
key_terms.تُبْتُ: I repented; his turning back to Allah from the sin
key_terms.حَجَجْتُ: I performed hajj; the act after which he met the Imam عليه السلام
key_terms.حُلَّ: undo; meaning to loosen or reverse what had been tied
key_terms.مَخْرَجٌ: a way out; a lawful exit from his previous occupation

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام say to a repentant sorcerer seeking a lawful way out?
ai.summary: This hadith relates the repentance of a man who had earned money through sorcery and sought guidance from Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام. The Imam’s reply indicates a lawful outlet in reversing harmful magic while forbidding initiating or performing it.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.3677 - It is narrated from Isa ibn Shaqafi, who was a sorcerer to whom people would come, and he used to take payment for it.
He said:

I performed Hajj and met Abu Abdillah (as) in Mina.
I said to Him (as): "May I be your ransom! I am a man whose profession was sorcery, and I used to take payment for it. I have performed Hajj, and Allah (swt), the Mighty and Exalted, has blessed me with meeting you, and I have repented to Allah (swt). Is there any way out for me regarding it?"
Imam (as) said: "Yes, undo (the spells) and do not tie (them)."
